title: How Sink Drainage Works: Gravity, Traps, and Venting
description: Sink drainage relies on a coordinated balance of gravity, liquid seals, and atmospheric pressure. When you open a faucet, wastewater flows downward through the tailpiece into the P-trap. The P-trap holds a standing pool of water that acts as a vital gas barrier, stopping sewer gases from entering living spaces. Downstream from the trap, the drain line connects to a vent stack that extends through the roof, equalizing air pressure so water can flow freely without gurgling or siphoning out the trap seal. Mastering this mechanical pathway is essential for every professional plumber.
